For six times something equals thirty, divide. The missing number is five.<break time="1s"/>Estimate with nearby tens. Thirty-seven rounds to forty; twenty-four rounds to twenty. Forty plus twenty makes sixty, so the total is about sixty. For whole numbers halfway between tens, round up.<break time="1s"/>Check this claim: twenty-seven plus eighteen equals thirty-five. What was missed?<break time="4s"/> The extra ten! The answer is forty-five. Also check the sign: five times four means twenty, not nine.<break time="1s"/>Understand the story, follow each step, and check your result. Put missing numbers back into their equations to test them. Try the Unit Two quizzes!</speak>
